summary.text: A 63-year-old man presented to the emergency department with a 1-month history of intermittent nausea, chills and jaundice. Preoperative laboratories showed elevated total bilirubin and alkaline phosphatase, normal CEA and elevated CA 19-9. MRI/MRCP showed proximal common bile duct thickening and biliary dilatation without distant disease, and incidentally showed gastrointestinal malrotation anatomy.

Biliary decompression was done by endoscopic retrograde cholangiography with endoprosthesis placement. At surgical exploration a proximal common bile duct mass without disseminated disease was found and malrotation was confirmed. The extrahepatic biliary tree was resected with portal lymphadenectomy and reconstructed with a Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy, with jejunal division and a right paracolic Roux limb tacked to the retroperitoneum.

Pathology showed a poorly differentiated common bile duct adenocarcinoma with negative margins and nodes. The postoperative course was complicated by prolonged ileus, with discharge home on postoperative day 16. He received 5-fluorouracil-based adjuvant chemotherapy and radiation therapy, developed recurrent malignant disease, and died 23 months postresection.

summary.text: A 47-year-old man presented to his primary care physician with a 3-month history of intermittent epigastric abdominal pain, nausea and vomiting. Liver function was normal, CEA was normal and CA 19-9 elevated. CT showed a 4.2 × 4.1 × 4 cm mass in the head and uncinate process of the pancreas, with the entire colon on the left and the small bowel on the right.

At operative exploration the SMA was rotated toward the uncinate process and encased by tumor, making the lesion unresectable. A palliative antiperistaltic gastrojejunostomy and Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy bypass were performed with the jejunal limb in a right paracolic position, and intraoperative biopsy showed a moderately differentiated PDA.

He received gemcitabine-based chemotherapy and radiation with successful downstaging, then underwent re-exploration and classic pancreaticoduodenectomy about 12 months after the initial exploration. Pathology showed PDA with perineural involvement at the uncinate margin and 3 of 13 positive nodes. He was discharged on postoperative day 8, developed recurrent malignant disease and died 10 months postresection.

summary.text: A 67-year-old Caucasian woman presented to her primary care physician with a 1-year history of epigastric abdominal pain, occasional nausea and emesis, and an unintentional 10 pound weight loss. CT showed a 4.5 × 4.1 cm periampullary pancreatic mass without evidence of metastatic disease and the colon dorsal to the SMA. Liver function tests and CEA were normal and CA 19-9 elevated.

At operative exploration the entire transverse colon was retroperitoneal and dorsal to the SMA and SMV, the duodenum coursed anterior to the mesenteric vessels, and a firm mass was in the pancreatic head. A classic pancreaticoduodenectomy was performed, and because of the retroperitoneal colon the jejunal limb was brought up in an antecolic position.

Pathology showed a moderately differentiated PDA with all margins free of tumor and 1 of 11 lymph nodes positive. She tolerated the procedure well and was discharged to home on postoperative day 5. She eventually developed recurrent disease and died 34 months postresection.
